payload.title: How to Get Married in Costa Rica Step by Step
payload.audience: 30s, couples who are interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, 150k+ AUD budget
payload.reader: An Australian couple in their 30s with a budget of AUD 150k or more, often with parents contributing, who have Costa Rica on the shortlist and want to know, before they commit to a resort or a coast, whether a Costa Rican ceremony is legally binding for them, which documents to gather first, who actually performs the civil marriage and how it is registered with the Registro Civil, how to make the certificate count back in Australia, and whether Guanacaste, the Central Pacific, the Caribbean coast or the Central Valley suits the wedding they picture. They want one calm, authoritative sequence, not a resort package list.
payload.goal: Book a Wedded Concierge consultation (speak with a Wedded Advisor) at /wonderland-concierge.
payload.angle: Page-one results for 'getting married in costa rica' are led by resort, package and local planner pages, with the legal side thin, undated, US-centred or copied between sites, and rarely clear on who performs the civil marriage or how it reaches the Registro Civil. This guide is written for Australians and in the order they have to act: whether they can marry legally in Costa Rica, only as official Costa Rican sources state; documents first, then entry; the Registro Civil (Tribunal Supremo de Elecciones) process step by step, including a lawyer-notary performing the civil marriage only if an official source says so; then the part resort pages skip, getting the certificate ready for Australia (Apostille through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and recognition, linked to our expert-advice pages); beach and outdoor ceremonies only as sourced, otherwise the questions a private, high-budget couple should put to a resort (sole use, security with a private team, privacy, deposits and contracts, step-free access); weather from the Instituto Meteorológico Nacional by station with dry and wet seasons as stated; and a business-free chooser across Guanacaste, the Central Pacific, the Caribbean and the Central Valley from the Instituto Costarricense de Turismo. Figure-free, dated once as at November 2026, fourth in the 'Getting Married in {Country}' series.
outline_spine: Intro: direct answer in the first 100 words (Australians can marry legally in Costa Rica by following the civil process recorded with the Registro Civil, as officially stated; this guide takes it step by step), then exactly 4 one-sentence takeaways.
Can Australians marry legally in Costa Rica? Civil ceremony and any religious ceremony only as official sources state; legal points dated once as at November 2026.

Documents first, then entry: documents the marriage officiant and Registro Civil ask for (CNI, translation or apostille of Australian documents only if stated), then entry from Smartraveller Costa Rica and official Costa Rican entry pages; no amounts or processing times.

Step by step: who may perform the civil marriage (a lawyer-notary only if an official source says so), any notice or waiting rules, appearances, witnesses, the ceremony, registration with the Registro Civil (TSE) and certificate copies; every step only as official pages state it; 'a fee applies' only where stated.

Getting your certificate ready for Australia: Apostille through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores y Culto, as sourced), translation from Spanish, recognition back home (Smartraveller, AGD); link the three expert-advice pages.

Beach and outdoor ceremonies: only what an official source states; otherwise questions to put to the resort on sole use, security with a private team, privacy, deposits and contracts, and step-free access; packages only as a question to ask.
When to marry: Instituto Meteorológico Nacional climate figures labelled by station; dry and wet seasons only as officially stated; no best month.
Choose your region: Guanacaste, Central Pacific, Caribbean and Central Valley, one or two lines each from the Instituto Costarricense de Turismo; no businesses, no ranking.
Venues and planning: one Wedded Advisor line from brand-facts.md (primary CTA); /magazine once; never legal paperwork help.
Close: plan your Costa Rica wedding with a Wedded Advisor (closing CTA).
must_include: Direct answer in the first 100 words that Australians can marry legally in Costa Rica by following the civil process as officially stated.
Exactly 4 Key takeaways, each one concise sentence, no figures, no prices.
The section spine above as H2s in sentence case, matching the series template order, no pasted or bracketed keywords.

Officiant, documents, notice or waiting rules, witnesses, Registro Civil registration and certificate copies only as official Costa Rican pages (TSE, Registro Civil) state them; lawyer-notary role only if officially sourced; 'as at November 2026' used once.

Australian recognition section linking /expert-advice/what-is-an-apostille-and-does-my-paperwork-need-one, /expert-advice/do-you-have-to-register-an-overseas-marriage-at-home and /expert-advice/overseas-marriage-certificate; Apostille issuer named only as sourced; never state Costa Rica requires a CNI unless an official source says so.
Resort questions on sole use, security with a private team, privacy, deposits and contracts, and step-free access where no official beach or outdoor rule is sourced.
Weather from the Instituto Meteorológico Nacional labelled by station; region lines for Guanacaste, Central Pacific, Caribbean and Central Valley only from the Instituto Costarricense de Turismo.

One Wedded Advisor line in the body plus the close, claims only from brand-facts.md 'Claims we can make' (single point of contact, works in your time zone and quotes in AUD, fee agreed in writing before work begins, inclusions confirmed in writing); /magazine once; series sisters /destination-weddings/getting-married-in-seychelles, /destination-weddings/mauritius-wedding and /destination-weddings/getting-married-in-hawaii linked once each.
avoid: Any price, fee amount, CRC, USD or AUD figure, 'from' price, percentage or processing time, including FAQ, meta and takeaways.
Packages described as offers or inclusions; packages appear only as a question to ask the resort.
'Best' anywhere (best region, best month, best resort).
Any statement of the legal position for same-sex couples.
Any Advisor or Wedded Wonderland role in legal paperwork, lawyer-notary arrangements, Registro Civil registration, apostilles or translations.
Wedded Privileges, room blocks, transfers, 'free', availability promises.
Resort, venue, vendor, lawyer, notary, officiant or planner names and any business or contact details (deferred).
Beach, maritime zone or national park ceremony rules not traced to an official page.
Any link to /destinations/latin-america-caribbean (do-not-link list, hidden from Google).
Research talk in copy (what we could or could not find, sources or method); hedge stacking.
Competitor wedding sites, resort or package sellers, directories, forums or Wikipedia as sources; competitor wording, claims or images (including Easy Weddings).
US spelling, em dashes, exclamation marks, cliches, 'last dance'.
AI images of any venue, destination or wedding.

key_takeaways_plan: Australians can have a legally binding wedding in Costa Rica by following the civil process and registration with the Registro Civil as it stands.
